messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — ran branching-sampling + q4_0 quant on llama3-12b-draft, attached microbench and small eval.

Maya: nice, what did you compare against? baseline beam or greedy?

Alex: greedy baseline quant (q4_0) and fp16 baseline on same infra. short log: 
```
model: llama3-12b-draft
mode: branching-sampling v1 (branch_factor=2, score_threshold=0.08)
quant: q4_0
inputs: 5k in-house regen prompts + 1k open benchmark subset
latency: p50=28ms/token, p95=90ms/token (single GPU)
throughput: 220 tok/s per GPU
cost: ~30% token compute reduction vs greedy q4_0
quality: ppl eval 4.9 vs baseline 4.7 (higher is worse)
A/B automated acceptability delta = -2.8%
```

Jordana: can you add KL and logp-diff distribution? ppl alone hides distributional shifts.

Alex: yep, quick numbers from the same run: avg token KL 0.12 nats, median logp-diff -0.03, top1-change rate 7.4% (i.e., different top token chosen vs baseline).

Chris: so ~30% perf gain but ~3% drop in acceptability. Any concentrated failures (safety, hallucination)?

Alex: most regressions are on multi-step reasoning QA and instruction-following examples with heavy constraints. hallucination rate up on long-context summarization by ~4.5%.

Maya: what was the eval set for acceptability? synthetic or human?

Alex: automated LLM-judge first pass (flan-judge, 3-shot), then we sampled 200 failed cases for quick human check — human confirmed ~60% of those were real regressions.

Lee: did you try tuning branching threshold or branch pruning to trade back quality?

Alex: tried threshold 0.06 and 0.1. 0.06 reduces regressions to -1.5% acceptability but latency p50 goes to 34ms/token. 0.1 gives stronger perf (p50 24ms) but acceptability -4.7%. 0.08 is the current sweet spot.

Jordana: request: add token-level KL per position (early vs late tokens). I suspect divergence spikes when cache warmup interacts with branching.

Alex: good point — per-position KL shows spike at tokens 1..6 (avg 0.25) then falls to 0.08 after 20 tokens. Branching pulls in alternate context early.

Chris: ops question — is this safe to canary? what rollback criteria?

Maya: suggest canary 5% traffic route with monitoring: acceptability delta (LLM-judge), human sample failure rate, latency p95, and error rate. auto-rollback if acceptability delta worse than -1.5% sustained for 30m.

CI-bot: regression-check: branching-sampling tests failed on test-suite 'instr-follow-basic' (4/200 failures). link: https://ci.internal/runs/2250001111

Alex: looking into those 4 failures now, probably threshold-sensitive prompts. will post a patch with tuned prune and additional unit tests. :mag:
